label: late original-phase token after a prefix rich in x/3/h/l/m/b/z/v/y/1
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at the delimiter or during copying, and never at positions 0-2. The rate climbs with position (orig_idx 3: 0.2%, 8: 9.4%), so most mass sits in the last 1-3 inputs before <DEL> of long sequences (L=8-9). It behaves like an accumulator over the prefix: it needs several earlier inputs from a history set {x,3,h,l,m,b,z,v,y,1} (first_tok x/3/h/l raises the rate about 3x), and the current input from a different set, mostly u (largest mass, and the top activations are all u), then 2, 0, o, f, c, d, n. It prefers first occurrences of the current token (in_first=0 carries only 10% of mass). The top activations are u at step 5-8 after prefixes like x 3 h ... / h 3 b x v. It does not fire on copy-phase steps, early positions, or when the current input is itself a history-set token. The boolean predicate only approximates what looks like a graded linear integration: dev F1 0.47, mass recall 0.77, and precision stays low (~0.36) because many matching contexts do not cross threshold. Seen 2/u earlier in the prefix appears to suppress it, but adding that condition did not help the score.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=x (+4.03), orig0=3 (+3.82), orig0=h (+3.61), orig0=l (+3.59), orig0=m (+3.39), orig0=b (+3.13). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-8.43), prev3_tok=- (-7.56), in_tok=v (-5.43), in_tok=h (-5.35).
